review: 2:1–2:2 אָשִׁיר לוֹ בְּכָל־עֵת / כָּל־עוֹד אָנִי קַיָּם — Psalm 104:33 (אָשִׁירָה לַיהוָה בְּחַיָּי); the Arabic أُغَنِّي لَهُ كُلَّ حِين / مَا دُمْتُ أَنَا فِي الْوُجُود is that resolve.
2:4 דּוֹד וְרַחוּם הוּא — 'Beloved and tender'; the Arabic الْحَبِيبُ وَالْوَدُود uses the two names, and וְרַחוּם is chosen as the biblical counterpart of الْوَدُود (Ex 34:6).
3:2 וְגַם בְּאַהֲבָתוֹ — 'matchless in His love'; the Arabic فَرِيد ('unique') has no adjective at four syllables, so the line states the love and leaves 'matchless' to the preceding נִפְלָא.
4:2 הַצֶּדֶק שָׁקַט כֵּן — 'justice was thus content'; the Arabic وَالْعَدْلُ هٰكَذَا اكْتَفَى is the satisfaction of justice, and שָׁקַט is the biblical verb for being at rest (Judg 3:11).
4:4 הוּא חֶלְקִי וְדַי — 'He is my portion — enough'; the Arabic فَهُوَ نَصِيبِي وَكَفَى is the same two-beat close, and דַּי is its exact Hebrew equivalent.
